requirement: Implement ImbalancedClassificationEvaluator class that computes balanced evaluation metrics (balanced accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and ROC-AUC), enforces binary label validation, ensures minority class sample quotas, and suppresses misleading raw accuracy when class imbalance exceeds a safety threshold.
skeleton: ImbalancedClassificationEvaluator class with threshold_probabilities and evaluate methods returning metric dictionaries.
caption: A scikit-learn evaluator for binary classifiers on heavily imbalanced data. ImbalancedClassificationEvaluator takes pos_label defaulting to 1, min_minority defaulting to 5, and imbalance_threshold defaulting to 5.0, raising ValueError when pos_label is not 0 or 1, when min_minority is below 1, and when the threshold is not above 1.0. threshold_probabilities raises ValueError for a threshold outside 0.0 to 1.0 and converts the probabilities with numpy and maps each one greater than or equal to the threshold to class 1 and the rest to 0. evaluate(y_true, y_pred=None, y_prob=None) derives predictions from probabilities when none are given and raises ValueError when both are missing, when the lengths differ, when any label or prediction falls outside the binary set 0 and 1, and when the minority class has fewer samples than min_minority, so exactly the minimum is accepted. It reports balanced_accuracy_score as balanced_accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 for pos_label from precision_recall_fscore_support with zero_division 0.0, and the majority-to-minority imbalance_ratio. When probabilities are supplied it adds roc_auc_score as roc_auc, inverted for positive label 0. Raw accuracy_score is added only while the imbalance ratio stays below the threshold. The fixture asserts that an all-zero predictor on skewed data gets zero recall, precision, and F1, balanced accuracy 0.5, and no accuracy key, that non-binary labels are rejected, that a perfect model at the minority minimum scores 1.0, and that a well-ranked model's roc_auc exceeds 0.95.

plan.intent: Evaluate a binary classifier honestly on imbalanced data
constraints: Invalid construction arguments, a threshold outside 0 to 1, missing predictions, mismatched lengths, non-binary labels, or too few minority samples raise ValueError
Probabilities at or above the threshold become class 1
Balanced accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 for the positive label are always reported
ROC AUC is added when probabilities are given
Plain accuracy is reported only while the imbalance ratio is below the threshold

rationale.teaches: Imbalance-aware evaluation: binary label validation, a minority quota, a probability threshold that maps to the positive class, balanced accuracy as the primary metric, and raw accuracy withheld above the imbalance threshold.
rationale.why: On a 95:5 dataset a constant classifier scores 95 percent raw accuracy. The fixture builds that dataset so the evaluator's choice of metric decides pass or fail.

ops.docstring: Score binary classifiers on imbalanced data without trusting raw accuracy.

candidates.why_wrong: pos_label defaults to 0, so precision, recall, and F1 are computed for the majority class.
The explicit binary check is gone, so a three-class input fails inside scikit-learn with an unrelated error instead of the documented binary message.
The minority quota uses <=, so exactly min_minority samples is rejected.
The threshold branch is inverted, so probabilities below the threshold become the positive class.
Raw accuracy is reported as the primary metric and balanced accuracy is omitted, so the imbalanced dataset looks excellent.
